messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: t-shirts?
parts:
I'm going to order some Stan t-shirts and need
to know what size everyone wants! And get feedback
on design.

I was thinking of something relatively simple
like the attached shots. I'm flexible on color,
size of logo, type of font, placement, etc. The
layout program on:

http://customink.com

is very flexible and the .pdf logo allows resizing
without aliasing. The one shown is a Hanes "Beefy
T" (they're heavyweight t-shirts), but they have a range
of options. The log is from the distro:

stan/logos/stanlogo-main.pdf

and the URL text is Arial. We could include more text,
but somehow "a C++ probability and sampling library"
seems too geeky.

I'm torn because I like darker t-shirts, but then I
prefer the logo non-reversed in terms of color. And I love
ringer Ts, but they only have Gildan, and then not in the
colors I really like.

They'll be around $11 each including
shipping if we order 20 of them and $9 each if we order 50.

For an extra $7/item, we can get our names and a number
on the back sports-jersey style (sorry Matt -- couldn't
resist).

- Bob

Would you prefer comic sans?

Small it is.

They actually do all kinds of sizes and shapes
of T-shirts, and they have t-shirts that on first
glance look like the light weight, long sleeve ones
you favor (but then it's maybe a Helvetica-Arial thing
and they just look superficially similar).

Here's the shop link:

http://www.customink.com

Their design tool's super easy. They'll be about
$10 each in bulk, but they're only $20 or so
one off. Michael B's used them and liked them.

I haven't ordered them yet because I needed to borrow
Illustrator from Daniel to adjust the vertical font spacing
on the Hamiltonian express.

I could generate more Helvetica in Illustrator
and then include it as an image. Would that
make you happier? They didn't offer a Helvetica
drop in on their site and I was just being
lazy.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: t-shirts?
parts:
T-shirts should be here early January -- I'm not
putting in a pre-Xmas rush order.

We can always order more if we like the first batch.
They're surprisingly inexpensive.

Thanks for the revised designs, Michael M! That would've
taken me yonks to figure out how to do in Illustrator.
I love that you did the professional visual balance of the text
under the logo --- circles are tricky because you can't literally
go to their edges. I also like the distance, which needs to be close
but not too close (sort of like caramel -- dark, but not too dark).
Our gain is the typography world's loss.

- Bob
